title: Dispatcher Board: clicking a day header in Schedule view opens Assign view for that date
tech: Node.js, TypeScript, Express, PostgreSQL, Prisma 6, Zod, Vitest, React 18, Vite, CSS Modules, Axios
keyConstraints: TypeScript strict mode, Zod validation server-side, .nullish() not .optional().nullable(), Prisma selects must include all returned fields (jobInclude is source of truth), no UI component libraries, CSS Modules only
description: In the Dispatcher Board Schedule view, clicking a day column header (e.g. 'FRI 10/7') switches the board to the Assign view with that date selected in the Assign view's existing date selection. This gives dispatchers a one-click path from spotting a day in the weekly schedule to assigning its jobs. The Assign view already has date selection — reuse it, do not build new filtering.
acceptanceCriteria: Clicking a day column header in Schedule view switches the Dispatcher Board to Assign view with that day set as the selected date, using the Assign view's existing date selection mechanism.
Only the day header is clickable for this action — clicks on job cards or the empty column body do not switch views.
Day headers show pointer cursor and a hover state; the header has an aria-label like 'Open assign view for {date}' translated via the existing i18n mechanism (EN/FI).
The Assign/Schedule toggle continues to work exactly as before, and switching back to Schedule view preserves the currently viewed week.
Works for all seven day columns including days with no jobs.
npx tsc --noEmit passes with no errors.
implementationNotes: VERIFY affectedFiles against the repo before implementing — check the actual component names for the Schedule and Assign views inside the Dispatcher Board and correct paths accordingly.

Inspect how the Assign view's existing date selection is stored (parent state in DispatcherBoard, URL param, or internal state) and pass the clicked date through that same mechanism — do not create a parallel date state.
Inspect how the Assign/Schedule toggle is stored and set it through the same mechanism when a day header is clicked.
Do not rewrite working code — add the header click handler and wiring only.
CSS Modules only — no inline styles.

Make the day header a real interactive element (button or role=button with tabIndex and Enter/Space key handling), and keep it structurally separate from any other click targets in the column to avoid stopPropagation workarounds.
Date passing must respect local timezone — the clicked day must equal the date selected in Assign view (no UTC off-by-one).
securityConsiderations: UI navigation only. No new endpoints, no new data exposure; Assign view keeps its existing role checks and data loading.
